question: Which two numbers (not digits) and which two signs should be interchanged to make the following equation correct? 33 - 15 × 4 + 9 ÷ 11 = 6
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/952c967501c582f1911db7fefdaaefa9b6e3f505512624eb925e04e002be5a1f.png] 

Given: 33 - 15 × 4 + 9 ÷ 11 = 6

According to the question, after interchanging the two numbers (not digits) and which two signs:

Option 1) 15 and 33, and ‘×’ and ‘÷’

33 - 15 × 4 + 9 ÷ 11 = 6 ⇒ 15 - 33 ÷ 4 + 9 × 11 = 6

⇒ 15 - __**33 ÷ 4**__ + 9 × 11 = 6

⇒ 15 - 8.25 + __**9 × 11**__ = 6

⇒ __**15 + 99**__ - 8.25 = 6

⇒ __**114 - 8.25**__ = 6

⇒ 105.75 ≠ 6 (LHS ≠ RHS)
